title: Generation and detection of squeezed light on a single silicon photonic chip
authors: Oliver M. Green, Bethany Puzio, Rowan A. Hoggarth, Rachel N. Clark, Edward C. R. Deacon, Alex S. Clark, Jonathan C. F. Matthews, Giacomo Ferranti
abstract: The ability to generate and detect quantum states of light on a single integrated photonic device is essential to scale quantum photonics into useful quantum technologies. Integrating the required capabilities into complementary-metal-oxide-semiconductor compatible monolithic chips can reduce cost and unlock new functionality through miniaturisation. In this work we demonstrate a single silicon-on-insulator photonic integrated circuit for the monolithic generation and detection of quantum light on a commercially available platform that operates entirely at room temperature. Specifically, we leverage spontaneous four-wave mixing in silicon waveguides to produce squeezed light which is subsequently detected by photodiodes operating in a pulsed homodyne detector configuration on the same chip as the source. We directly measure $0.25(1)$ dB of squeezing, including contributions from waveguide propagation loss and detection inefficiency, and include a detailed analysis of the impact of nonlinear loss on the squeezing levels achievable using this platform.
summary: The paper reports on the successful demonstration of generating and detecting squeezed light entirely on a single silicon photonic chip. By integrating the nonlinear source (SFWM) and the homodyne detector onto one SOI platform, they overcome previous limitations in footprint and complexity. This work advances the feasibility of scalable, room-temperature quantum photonic devices for applications like quantum sensing.
main_problem: The necessity of generating and detecting quantum states of light on a single integrated photonic device to scale quantum photonics into useful technologies.
main_result: The authors demonstrated the monolithic generation and detection of squeezed light on a silicon-on-insulator chip, achieving a measured squeezing level of 0.25(1) dB.
method: Squeezed light was generated via spontaneous four-wave mixing in a silicon waveguide and detected using an integrated pulsed homodyne detector configuration.
model_or_system: The platform is a single monolithic Silicon-on-Insulator (SOI) photonic integrated circuit, which integrates the nonlinear source (SFWM) and the detection apparatus (homodyne detector) at room temperature.
key_observables: Measured squeezing level (0.25(1) dB), inferred entering squeezing (0.42(2) dB), total generated squeezing (0.83(3) dB), and nonlinear refractive index ($n_2$).
important_parameters: Room temperature operation, monolithic integration footprint ($	ext{1.44 mm}^2$), pulsed laser source.
main_assumptions: The analysis includes detailed consideration of contributions from waveguide propagation loss and detection inefficiency; the primary limitation noted is intrinsic nonlinear loss in SOI waveguides.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the PIC layout, the dual-pump preparation scheme involving multiple optical components (WaveShapers, MZI), and the measurement process showing sinusoidal variance variation with LO phase and dependence on pump power.
paper_structure: The work details the physical setup using an SOI chip for monolithic operation. It covers the generation mechanism (SFWM), the complex detection scheme (pulsed homodyne detector with AMZIs), rigorous characterization of squeezing via quadrature measurements, and analysis of loss mechanisms.
why_interesting: This is highly relevant as it provides a concrete, scalable platform for continuous-variable quantum optics experiments, directly addressing integration challenges crucial for building quantum networks or sensors.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The photonic chip (a) Layout of the SOI photonic integrated circuit (PIC). A bi-chromatic pump and local oscillator (LO) couple into the PIC via separate grating couplers. The pump generates degenerate squeezing, as shown in the insert, by spontaneous four-wave mixing in a spiral waveguide. Two cascaded asymmetric Mach Zehnder interferometers (AMZIs) separate squeezed light from pump. The former is then routed to the on-chip homodyne detector, composed of waveguide- coupled germanium photodiodes at each output of a Mach Zehnder interferometer (MZI). The LO field couples directly from its input grating coupler into the homodyne MZI, where it interferes with the squeezed light. (b)...

FIG. 2. Dual-pump preparation scheme (a) Schematic of the experiment, divided into four stages. Pulse preparation: Three spectral lines carved by the WaveShaper from a spectrally-broad pulsed pump enter an erbium-doped fibre amplifier (EDFA). Delay matching: The three wavelengths are demultiplexed (DEMUX) and tunable delay lines correct the temporal mismatch between them. Pumps P1 and P2 are recombined in a wavelength multiplexer (MUX) to act as a bi-chromatic pump field. A variable optical attenuator (VOA) sets the pump intensity which is monitored by a 99:1 splitter and a power meter (POW). A VOA and phase modulator (ϕ) are used to control the power and phase of the local oscillator (LO)....

FIG. 3. Squeezed light measurement (a) The evolution of the variance of the signal recorded on the integrated homodyne detector as the LO phase is swept, exhibiting clear sub-shot noise fluctuations reaching 0.25(1) dB of squeezing. (b) The dependence of the squeezing (purple circles) and antisqueezing (green squares) generated and detected on chip as peak pump power is varied, reaching a maximum detected squeezing level of 0.25(1) dB. The data is fitted with the theoretical scaling from Eq. 2. An extension of the fit to higher optical powers (dashed lines) shows generated squeezing saturates due to the effects of nonlinear loss.
